newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police clash with anti-drug campaigners.
newsitem.headline: S.African police clash with anti-drug campaigners.

text.p: South African police clashed with Moslems campaigning against drugs at a popular shopping centre on Sunday, opening fire with rubber bullets when some protesters began pelting officers with bottles.
At least one man was seriously hurt in the fracas, and had to be taken to hospital. Two paramedics and several policemen also sustained slight injuries.
The afternoon demonstration by men, women and children aligned to the Moslem-dominated People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad) movement started peacefully.
But scuffles broke out when police, heavily armed and in full riot gear, used their batons to break up the crowd and began arresting some of the protesters.
"There was an illegal gathering here. They were asked to disperse, and given five minutes to do so. They did not," a police spokesman, Captain Wicus Holtzhausen, told Reuters.
"Police started arresting them. That was when they started throwing bottles and then the police fired rubber bullets," he said.
Holtzhausen said he could not immediately tally the number of people arrested or hurt. "We don't know the numbers yet but quite a few of them were arrested," he added.

Last month, 28 people were hurt when police used rubber bullets and birdshot to disperse a crowd which tossed stones at policemen in a demonstration against drug dealers at Clanwilliam, about 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Cape Town.
Crowds of vigilantes threatening to kill drug barons who do not give up their trade have repeatedly confronted police during marches to the homes of alleged dealers around South Africa.
In August militant Moslems affiliated to the Pagad movement publicly shot and burned to death an alleged drug merchant and gang leader near Cape Town.
